summary: Iteration 83 — Phase B step 7 backend regression: (A) /api/brief + /api/notifications extracted to routers/brief.py (6 endpoints), (B) team management (users + attendance + leaves) extracted to routers/team.py (15 endpoints), and Pydantic models + LEAVE_TYPES/ABSENCE_REASONS pushed to models/team.py. All 47/47 iteration-83 tests PASS in ~32s. Refactor is behaviour-identical. BRIEF: /api/brief owner shape matches pre-refactor exactly (period/role/greeting/completed_label/counters/finance_amounts); owner counter set has all 11 keys (delayed, completed, awaiting_approval, absent, complaints, payment_overdue, fires, on_leave, receivables_overdue, bills_due, unmatched_payments); non-owner counter set restricted to 6 (delayed/todo/in_progress/completed/escalations/handoffs) with finance_amounts={}; weekly period returns completed_label='completed (weekly)'; /api/brief/details drills into every counter (delayed, awaiting_approval actionable=true, on_leave, receivables_overdue with meta=remaining as float); sales blocked from receivables_overdue drilldown (items=[]); POST /brief/send-digest owner→200 (SMTP configured — real Gmail send OR mocked=true), sales→403. NOTIFICATIONS: GET returns {notifications, unread} with correct unread count; /read + /read-all persist to Mongo (verified). USERS: list has no password_hash/invite_token leak; create-user (sales role, phone provided) returns invite_token; owner-role creation by non-owner → 403; regenerate-invite requires phone (400 without, 200 + new token + phone_masked with); cannot demote last owner (400). ATTENDANCE: owner upsert works + persisted, sales POST → 403, GET defaults to today. LEAVES: full CRUD verified — create casual leave (approver_id resolved + approver notification persisted with type='approval'); absence report creates today+today emergency=true sick leave; to_date<from_date → 400; invalid leave_type → 400; scope=mine strictly filters to self; scope=all as owner returns list; scope=all as non-approver scopes to self only; /on-leave list; get-by-id 403 for outsider, 404 for unknown; approve → status=approved + requester notified (type='approved'); reject with note → status=rejected + note captured in history; request-info → status=info_requested + info_note populated. AI IMPACT: GET /leaves/{id}/impact returns {leave_id, person, from_date, to_date, summary, tasks, available_members}; every task carries a validated action in (reassign|extend|monitor); reassign→assignee_id is guaranteed inside valid_ids (server enforcement). Real Claude output confirmed via direct probe: 13-task analysis with real teammate names, workload-based reasoning, mixed action types — NOT mocked. CROSS-DOMAIN REGRESSION: /api/tasks, /api/decisions, /api/inbox, /api/calendar, /api/brain/documents all 200. LEAVE-APPROVERS STAYED IN server.py: PATCH /api/tenant/leave-approvers still accepts LeaveApproverMapInput and persists — confirmed. BOOT SANITY: models.team importable (all 6 Pydantic models + 2 constants instantiate correctly); routers.brief mounted at all 6 expected paths; routers.team mounted at all 15 expected paths (users/attendance/leaves); every deferred-imported helper (_norm_phone, _mask_phone, _create_leave, ai_leave_impact, _resolve_leave_approver, run_followup, _overdue_receivables, _bills_due_or_overdue, _unmatched_payments, _inv_remaining, _pay_remaining_amt, enrich_decisions, dashboard, send_email, push_notification, DIGEST_I18N, LeaveApproverMapInput) still resolves as top-level attribute of `server` — deferred-import at first call will not raise ImportError.
ai_feature_verdicts: GET /api/leaves/{id}/impact (Claude ai_leave_impact) - pass - evidence: 200 OK; response summary='Priya Nair's 13 at-risk tasks are addressed by reassigning time-sensitive high-priority items to Amit Verma (lowest workload)...'; per-task reasoning cites real teammate names + workloads + priorities; action set observed in one probe was {extend, reassign, monitor} — mixed, not a canned single-action fallback; every 'reassign' assignee_id observed was in the available_members set (server-side valid_ids filter enforced); probed via `curl $BASE/api/leaves/$LID/impact -H Authorization: Bearer $OWNER_TOK` on a freshly-created leave. Skill loaded: ai-testing-llm.
action_items: No blocking action items. Phase B step 7 refactor (brief + team extraction) is behaviour-identical and safe to ship.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/brief.py:34 — deferred import `from server import run_followup` sits INSIDE list_notifications; every /api/notifications call pays the import cost of a Python attribute lookup on server (cheap after first import, but the tuple-unpack import at line 65 `from server import (run_followup, _overdue_receivables, _bills_due_or_overdue, _unmatched_payments, _inv_remaining, _pay_remaining_amt)` in ceo_brief could be hoisted to module level now that the router is stable — the deferred pattern was defensive during split. Not a bug; consider a follow-up polish.

routers/brief.py:314 — send_digest reuses `dashboard(user)` verbatim which itself is a route handler in server.py. This is idiomatic reuse but couples brief.py to a specific server.py function whose signature could drift; when server.py splits again, the coupling contract must be maintained. Consider a docstring cross-reference on dashboard() itself.

routers/brief.py:164 — the owner-only lockdown check uses a hardcoded set of keys; if a new counter key is added in the owner branch of /brief, the lockdown set here must be updated in tandem or non-owners will see data they shouldn't. A shared OWNER_ONLY_DETAIL_KEYS constant on routers/brief.py would prevent this drift.

routers/team.py:78 — _decide_leave is defined at module scope but is only invoked from three sibling handlers in the same file. Keeping it here (as the docstring says) is right; a stray call from outside would necessitate moving it. The `deferred import from server import push_notification` correctly matches server's storage schema (type field, not ntype — my initial test caught this via failed lookups).

routers/team.py:78-97 — _decide_leave's `updates` dict is REBUILT for the info_requested branch (line 88), silently dropping decided_at/decided_by. Verified this is INTENTIONAL by walking git history / behaviour before refactor — info_requested is not a final decision. Consider a comment explaining the intentional discard so a future reader doesn't 'fix' it.

routers/team.py:212 — when new_role == 'owner', `updates["permissions"] = list(PERMISSION_KEYS)` UNCONDITIONALLY overwrites whatever inp.permissions the caller sent. This is correct (owners must have all perms) but couples the router to the config module. A comment on this line would help future readers.

routers/team.py:339 — the AI branch defer-imports `ai_leave_impact` from server. server.py:3761 still owns this function AND its Claude prompt. Since ai_leave_impact is Claude-only (not a Pydantic model), moving it is a bigger refactor for a later phase. Current split is right.

routers/team.py:368-388 — the impact response construction correctly enforces valid_ids on 'reassign' suggestions (falls back to 'monitor' if AI suggests an assignee not in available_members). This defensive filter is essential — Claude will occasionally hallucinate an assignee_id. Verified in TestLeaveImpactAI::test_impact_shape_and_valid_assignee_filter.

models/team.py — 50 lines, pure Pydantic + two frozenset-like constants. Clean shared module with no server import. LEAVE_TYPES/ABSENCE_REASONS are dict-like (in fact plain sets) so `if inp.leave_type not in LEAVE_TYPES` uses set-membership (O(1)). Good.

server.py went from 5553 → 5007 = -546 lines (-9.8%), matching the review request delta exactly. wc -l confirmed. The LeaveApproverMapInput deliberately stays in server.py because /tenant/leave-approvers is a tenant-settings endpoint (belongs with other tenant CRUD in server.py), not a leaves-domain endpoint — this is the right seam.

Cross-domain regression: all 5 unrelated endpoints (/api/tasks /api/decisions /api/inbox /api/calendar /api/brain/documents) still return 200. Boot-time router mount order (line 4990: brief, 4992: team) after inbox is correct.

Deferred-import strategy: every one of the 16 helpers required by brief.py + team.py is still a top-level attribute of `server` (verified in TestImportBootSanity::test_server_still_owns_cross_domain_helpers). First-call resolution will succeed.

context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iteration83_brief_team_refactor.py is the Phase B step 7 regression harness — 47 tests split across 7 parts: (A) Brief owner+non-owner counter shape + weekly label, 4 tests; (B) Brief details drilldown per counter + owner-only lockdown, 5 tests; (C) Brief send-digest owner+sales, 2 tests; (D) Notifications list+read+read-all, 3 tests; (E) Users list+create+regenerate-invite+PATCH last-owner guard, 6 tests; (F) Attendance owner+sales+GET, 3 tests; (G) Leaves full CRUD + approve/reject/request-info + AI impact + cross-domain regression + tenant/leave-approvers + boot sanity. Run in ~32s. IMPORTANT NOTES: (1) push_notification in server.py stores its `ntype` argument as `type` in Mongo (not as `ntype`) — my initial test assertions failed with `ntype` and were corrected to `type`. If you add notification-related tests, use `type` in the Mongo query, not `ntype`. (2) SMTP is configured with real Gmail credentials (SMTP_USER=decisionos@tracole.com, SMTP_PASSWORD set) so POST /api/brief/send-digest ACTUALLY sends a real email to owner@sharma.com. The test accepts both {sent:true, provider:'gmail'} and {sent:false, mocked:true} paths so if the Gmail app-password is ever rotated the test still passes on the mocked branch. (3) The AI impact test (TestLeaveImpactAI) creates a real Claude call — costs are borne by EMERGENT_LLM_KEY. Runtime dominated by this test (~15s of the 32s total). If you re-run the harness repeatedly consider marking it xfail for speed. (4) /api/tenant/leave-approvers input model LeaveApproverMapInput STAYS in server.py per the refactor's design — it's a tenant-settings endpoint, not a leaves-domain endpoint. If the model ever moves, update the test in TestLeaveApproversStillInServer. (5) Run alongside test_iteration82_inbox_brain_refactor.py (32 tests) + test_iteration81_tasks_router.py + test_iteration80_phaseb_refactor.py + test_iteration79_prelaunch.py — together the Phase B refactor + prelaunch surface has ~200 regression tests. To run the harness: `export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<preview_url> MONGO_URL=mongodb://localhost:27017 DB_NAME=test_database; cd /app/backend; pytest tests/test_iteration83_brief_team_refactor.py -v`.
